## Executive Summary

This document geocodes the **26 sentinel sites** of the DRC surveillance network — one per province — deriving latitude and longitude for each `sentinel_site` using its `province` as a constraint.

It produces coordinates with full provenance for every site, a review queue of anything that could not be trusted outright, and an interactive map for visual verification.

### Administrative Hierarchy

| Level | Field | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| Country | — | Democratic Republic of the Congo |
| Admin 1 | `province` | Province (current 26-province configuration) |
| Health Zone | `sentinel_site` | Zone de Santé hosting the sentinel site |
| Identifier | `site_id` | Derived from the site name, e.g. `DRC-VANGA` |

### Design principles

1. **Constrain, then verify.** The province is pinned server-side with Google's `components=country:CD|administrative_area:<province>` filter rather than appended to a query string. That filter is advisory rather than binding, so the province is also **checked against the response** before a result is accepted.
2. **Judge matches on the API's own quality signals.** Calling the REST endpoint directly exposes `partial_match`, `location_type`, `types` and the result count. These drive the quality gate, instead of inferring quality from whether a coordinate came back at all.
3. **Refuse rather than downgrade.** A candidate in the wrong province, or whose name bears no resemblance to the site, is discarded and the ladder keeps walking. For spatial analysis a wrong coordinate is worse than a missing one.

### Background

Accurate geolocation of sentinel sites supports:

- Spatial analysis of disease transmission patterns
- Healthcare accessibility modelling
- Intervention planning and optimisation
- Care seeking and delivery modelling

## System Requirements

### R Package Installation

```{r}
#| label: package-installation
#| eval: false

# Core packages required
packages <- c(
  "tidyverse",     # Data manipulation
  "httr",          # HTTP requests
  "jsonlite",      # JSON parsing
  "leaflet",       # Map visualization
  "htmlwidgets",   # Save interactive widgets
  "knitr"          # For this documentation
)

# Installation function
install_if_missing <- function(packages) {
  missing <- packages[!(packages %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"])]
  if(length(missing) > 0) {
    install.packages(missing, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org/")
  }
}

install_if_missing(packages)
```

Dependencies are managed with `renv` where a lockfile is available: if a
`renv.lock` sits in the parent directory, run `renv::restore()` from there
before rendering. Otherwise install the packages above directly with
`install.packages()`. See `README.md` for the full setup.

```{r}
#| label: load-libraries
#| eval: true

library(tidyverse)
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(leaflet)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(knitr)

source("config.R")
source("geocode-functions.R")

dir.create(paths$output, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

### API Credentials

The Google Maps Geocoding API requires a key with the **Geocoding API** enabled
(<https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials>). It is read from the
`GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` environment variable and is never printed or written to
any output file.

```{r}
#| label: api-key-check
#| eval: true

google_api_key <- Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY")

if (nchar(google_api_key) == 0) {
  stop("GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is not set. Export it before rendering this document.")
}

cat("Google Maps API key detected (", nchar(google_api_key), " characters).\n", sep = "")
```

## Province Validation

The input uses the **current 26-province** configuration created by the 2015
reorganisation, which is the structure reflected in Google's — and
OpenStreetMap's — administrative data. Each province appears exactly once, with
one sentinel site.

This matters because the province is not merely appended to a query string: it
is pinned as a `components` filter and then checked against the response. A
pre-2015 name (Bandundu, Katanga, Orientale, Bas-Congo, Kasaï-Occidental) or a
typo would silently weaken that constraint on every query for the affected
site, so the input is validated against the canonical list before any request
is made.

Note that the input spells provinces inconsistently — `Kasaï` carries its
diaeresis while `Bas-Uele` does not. Comparison runs through `normalise_name()`,
which folds accents and punctuation, so no cleaning is required.

```{r}
#| label: province-list
#| eval: true

tibble(Province = drc_provinces) |>
  mutate(n = row_number()) |>
  select(n, Province) |>
  kable(caption = "The 26 provinces the input is validated against")
```

## Geocoding Methodology

### The Query Ladder

Each site is resolved by walking an ordered ladder of query variants and
stopping at the first candidate that passes the quality gate. The rung that
succeeded is recorded, so it is visible afterwards how hard the geocoder had to
work.

| Rung | `address` | `components` |
|------|-----------|--------------|
| 1 | `Zone de Sante de {site}` | `country:CD\|administrative_area:{province}` |
| 2 | `{site}` | `country:CD\|administrative_area:{province}` |
| 3 | `{site}, {province}, Republique Democratique du Congo` | `country:CD` |
| 4 | `{site}` | `country:CD` |

Rungs 1 and 2 pin the province server-side. Rung 3 drops that constraint but
keeps the province as a search term. Rung 4 is a last resort restricted only by
country.

Four requests per site at worst — around 100 in total, well inside the free
monthly tier.

```{r}
#| label: query-ladder-example
#| eval: true

build_query_variants("Vanga", "Kwilu") |>
  select(rung, address, components) |>
  kable(caption = "The ladder for one site")
```

### The Quality Gate

A candidate is **rejected outright** — discarded, with the ladder continuing —
when any of the following hold:

1. `location_type == "APPROXIMATE"` *and* its `types` include
   `administrative_area_level_1`, `administrative_area_level_2` or `country`.
   The geocoder returned a province or district centroid rather than the site.
2. Its coordinates fall outside the DRC bounding box.
3. **The returned `administrative_area_level_1` is not the province asked for.**
4. **The returned name bears no resemblance to the site name** — similarity
   below `r gate$similarity_floor`.

Rules 3 and 4 exist because of a real failure. In testing against the live API,
a query pinned to `administrative_area:Kasai` came back with
*"Avenue TP numéro 3C, Quartier Funa, Kinshasa"* — a business roughly 700 km
from Kasaï — and the gate accepted it. Two lessons followed:

- Google's `administrative_area` component filter is **advisory, not binding**,
  so the province must be verified in the response.
- Name similarity separates good from bad cleanly: every correct match scored
  **1.00**, while the two wrong ones scored **0.56** and **0.25**.

Note what is deliberately *not* a rule: a blacklist on `establishment` or
`point_of_interest` types. Both bad results carried them — but so would a
legitimate match on "Centre de Santé de …", so the type alone proves nothing.

Surviving candidates carry **soft flags** that set the confidence tier: more
than one result returned, an unverifiable province, an imperfect name match, or
a `partial_match` *combined with* a weak name. That last qualifier matters —
`partial_match` fires on every rung-1 query simply because the result does not
contain the literal `"Zone de Sante de "` prefix, and counting it unconditionally
made `high` confidence unreachable for every site in the earlier run.

| Tier | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `high` | Resolved at rung 1–2 with no flags |
| `medium` | Resolved at rung 1–3 with at most one flag |
| `low` | Accepted, but with several doubts — review before use |
| `manual` | Coordinates pinned by an analyst in `manual_overrides.csv` |
| `failed` | No candidate survived the gate |

Everything below `high` is written to a review file. A site that **fails** is
working as intended: it means no candidate could be trusted, and the location
should be pinned by hand rather than guessed.

## Data Preparation

```{r}
#| label: data-preparation
#| eval: true

sites <- read.csv(paths$input, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  ensure_site_id() |>
  distinct(site_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

cat("=====================================\n")
cat("DRC SENTINEL SITE GEOCODING\n")
cat("Geocoding Service: Google Maps Geocoding API\n")
cat("=====================================\n\n")
cat("Total sites to geocode:", nrow(sites), "\n")
cat("Unique provinces (adm1):", length(unique(sites$province)), "\n\n")

# Reject pre-2015 province names and typos before spending any requests: either
# would silently weaken the province constraint on every query for that site.
validate_provinces(sites)
cat("All", length(unique(sites$province)),
    "provinces are current 26-province names.\n")

sites |>
  select(site_id, province, sentinel_site) |>
  head(5) |>
  kable(caption = "First five sites, with derived identifiers")
```

```{r}
#| label: cache-init
#| eval: true

n_cached <- cache_load()
cat("Cached responses available:", n_cached, "\n")
```

## Main Processing Loop

```{r}
#| label: processing-loop
#| eval: true

results <- list()
audits  <- list()
start_time <- Sys.time()

cat("\nStarting geocoding process with the Google Maps Geocoding API...\n")
cat("================================================================\n\n")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(sites))) {

  site_row <- sites[i, ]

  out <- geocode_site(
    site_id  = site_row$site_id,
    site     = site_row$sentinel_site,
    province = site_row$province
  )

  results[[i]] <- out$result
  audits[[i]]  <- out$audit

  elapsed <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins"))
  cat(sprintf("[%2d/%2d] %-12s %-18s -> %-7s (rung %s) | %.2f min elapsed\n",
              i, nrow(sites),
              site_row$sentinel_site,
              site_row$province,
              out$result$confidence,
              ifelse(is.na(out$result$resolved_at_rung), "-", out$result$resolved_at_rung),
              elapsed))
}

geocoded  <- bind_rows(results)
candidates <- bind_rows(audits)

cache_save()

total_time <- difftime(Sys.time(), start_time, units = "mins")

cat("\nGeocoding complete.\n")
cat("Total time:", round(total_time, 2), "minutes\n")
cat("API calls made:", .geocode_cache$calls, "| served from cache:", .geocode_cache$hits, "\n\n")
```

## Manual Overrides

Sites the geocoder gets wrong are corrected by adding a row to
`../input/manual_overrides.csv` (`site_id, latitude, longitude, note`) and
re-rendering. Overrides take precedence over any API result and are stamped
`geocode_status = "manual"`.

```{r}
#| label: manual-overrides
#| eval: true

n_before <- sum(geocoded$geocode_status == "manual")
geocoded <- apply_manual_overrides(geocoded)
n_after  <- sum(geocoded$geocode_status == "manual")

cat("Manual overrides applied:", n_after - n_before, "\n")
```

## Data Export

```{r}
#| label: data-export
#| eval: true

# Preserve every input column, then attach coordinates and provenance
final <- sites |>
  left_join(geocoded, by = "site_id") |>
  mutate(
    latitude  = as.numeric(latitude),
    longitude = as.numeric(longitude)
  )

write.csv(final, file.path(paths$output, "drc_sentinel_sites_geocoded.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
cat("Main results saved to: output/drc_sentinel_sites_geocoded.csv\n")

# Full audit trail: every candidate seen at every rung, accepted or not
write.csv(candidates, file.path(paths$output, "drc_geocoding_candidates.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
cat("Candidate audit trail saved to: output/drc_geocoding_candidates.csv\n")

# Anything short of a clean high-confidence match
review <- final |> filter(!confidence %in% c("high", "manual"))
write.csv(review, file.path(paths$output, "drc_geocoding_review.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
cat("Review queue (", nrow(review), " sites) saved to: output/drc_geocoding_review.csv\n", sep = "")

failed <- final |> filter(is.na(latitude) | is.na(longitude))
write.csv(failed, file.path(paths$output, "drc_geocoding_failed.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
cat("Failed cases (", nrow(failed), " sites) saved to: output/drc_geocoding_failed.csv\n", sep = "")
```

## Results Analysis

### Success Metrics

```{r}
#| label: success-metrics
#| eval: true

summary_stats <- final |>
  summarise(
    total_sites  = n(),
    geocoded     = sum(!is.na(latitude)),
    failed       = sum(is.na(latitude)),
    success_rate = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * sum(!is.na(latitude)) / n())
  )

cat("\n=====================================\n")
cat("RESULTS SUMMARY\n")
cat("=====================================\n\n")
cat("Total sites:", summary_stats$total_sites, "\n")
cat("Successfully geocoded:", summary_stats$geocoded, "\n")
cat("Failed:", summary_stats$failed, "\n")
cat("Success rate:", summary_stats$success_rate, "\n\n")

final |>
  count(confidence, name = "sites") |>
  arrange(match(confidence, c("high", "medium", "low", "manual", "failed"))) |>
  kable(caption = "Confidence tiers")
```

### Which Rung Resolved Each Site

Most sites should resolve at rung 1 or 2, where the province is pinned. Heavy
reliance on rungs 3–4 means the province-constrained queries are not finding
these health zones and the site names may need correcting in `site_name_fixes`.

```{r}
#| label: rung-analysis
#| eval: true

final |>
  select(sentinel_site, province, matched_admin1, resolved_at_rung,
         confidence, location_type) |>
  arrange(resolved_at_rung, sentinel_site) |>
  kable(caption = "Resolution rung by site")

final |>
  count(resolved_at_rung, name = "sites") |>
  kable(caption = "Sites resolved per rung")
```

### Provincial Breakdown

```{r}
#| label: provincial-analysis
#| eval: true

by_province <- final |>
  group_by(province) |>
  summarise(
    total        = n(),
    geocoded     = sum(!is.na(latitude)),
    success_rate = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * sum(!is.na(latitude)) / n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total), province)

# With one sentinel site per province this collapses to a column of 1s, so it
# is only worth printing once a province carries more than one site.
if (max(by_province$total) > 1) {
  kable(by_province, caption = "Success rate by province")
} else {
  cat("One sentinel site per province, so a provincial breakdown adds nothing\n")
  cat("beyond the confidence and rung tables above.\n")
}
```

## Data Quality Checks

### Coordinate Bounds

```{r}
#| label: coordinate-validation
#| eval: true

bb <- country_profile$bbox

out_of_bounds <- final |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude)) |>
  filter(latitude  < bb$lat_min | latitude  > bb$lat_max |
         longitude < bb$lon_min | longitude > bb$lon_max)

cat("Coordinate validation (DRC bounds: lat ", bb$lat_min, " to ", bb$lat_max,
    ", lon ", bb$lon_min, " to ", bb$lon_max, ")\n", sep = "")
cat("Sites within bounds:", sum(!is.na(final$latitude)) - nrow(out_of_bounds), "\n")
cat("Sites outside bounds:", nrow(out_of_bounds), "\n")

if (nrow(out_of_bounds) > 0) {
  write.csv(out_of_bounds, file.path(paths$output, "drc_out_of_bounds.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  cat("Out-of-bounds sites saved to: output/drc_out_of_bounds.csv\n")
}
```

### Duplicate Coordinates

Two sites sharing a coordinate almost always means a fallback to a shared
administrative centroid slipped past the quality gate.

```{r}
#| label: duplicate-coordinates
#| eval: true

dupes <- final |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
  count(latitude, longitude, name = "n_sites") |>
  filter(n_sites > 1)

if (nrow(dupes) == 0) {
  cat("No duplicate coordinates. Every site resolved to a distinct point.\n")
} else {
  cat("WARNING:", nrow(dupes), "coordinate pair(s) shared by more than one site.\n")
  final |>
    semi_join(dupes, by = c("latitude", "longitude")) |>
    select(sentinel_site, province, latitude, longitude, matched_address) |>
    arrange(latitude, longitude) |>
    kable()
}
```

### Province Agreement

Confirms the gate held. A province mismatch is now a hard rejection, so every
geocoded site must report the province it was asked for — any `FALSE` below
would mean rule 3 of the quality gate is not firing.

```{r}
#| label: province-agreement
#| eval: true

agreement <- final |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), geocode_status != "manual") |>
  mutate(agrees = normalise_name(matched_admin1) == normalise_name(province)) |>
  select(sentinel_site, province, matched_admin1, agrees)

n_bad <- sum(!agreement$agrees, na.rm = TRUE)

if (n_bad == 0) {
  cat("All", nrow(agreement),
      "geocoded sites returned the province they were constrained to.\n\n")
} else {
  cat("WARNING:", n_bad, "site(s) returned a different province than requested.\n")
  cat("The quality gate should have rejected these -- investigate.\n\n")
}

agreement |>
  arrange(agrees, sentinel_site) |>
  kable(caption = "Requested vs returned province")
```

### Spot Check

With 26 sites, every point can and should be verified by eye. Each row links to
the exact coordinate on Google Maps and OpenStreetMap. Pay closest attention to
the urban health zones — Kabondo (a commune of Kisangani), Dibindi (Mbuji-Mayi)
and Kingasani (Kinshasa) — which are not standalone settlements and are the most
likely to resolve to something plausible but wrong.

```{r}
#| label: spot-check
#| eval: true

final |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude)) |>
  transmute(
    Site       = sentinel_site,
    Province   = province,
    Matched    = matched_address,
    Confidence = confidence,
    Coordinates = sprintf("%.4f, %.4f", latitude, longitude),
    Verify = sprintf(
      "[Google](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=%f,%f) / [OSM](https://www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat=%f&mlon=%f#map=12/%f/%f)",
      latitude, longitude, latitude, longitude, latitude, longitude
    )
  ) |>
  kable()
```

## Visualization

```{r}
#| label: map-creation
#| eval: true

mapped <- final |> filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude))

if (nrow(mapped) > 0) {

  pal <- colorFactor(palette = "viridis", domain = mapped$province)

  map <- leaflet(mapped) |>
    addTiles() |>
    addCircleMarkers(
      ~longitude, ~latitude,
      group = ~confidence,
      popup = ~paste0(
        "<b>", sentinel_site, "</b><br>",
        "<b>Site ID:</b> ", site_id, "<br>",
        "<b>Province (input):</b> ", province, "<br>",
        "<b>Province (returned):</b> ", matched_admin1, "<br>",
        "<b>Matched address:</b> ", matched_address, "<br>",
        "<b>Confidence:</b> ", confidence, " (rung ", resolved_at_rung, ")<br>",
        "<b>Location type:</b> ", location_type, "<br>",
        "<b>Coordinates:</b> ", round(latitude, 4), ", ", round(longitude, 4)
      ),
      label = ~sentinel_site,
      labelOptions = labelOptions(noHide = TRUE, direction = "top",
                                  textOnly = TRUE,
                                  style = list("font-weight" = "bold")),
      color = ~pal(province),
      radius = 7,
      fillOpacity = 0.8
    ) |>
    addLegend(
      "bottomright",
      pal = pal,
      values = ~province,
      title = "Province",
      opacity = 1
    ) |>
    addLayersControl(
      overlayGroups = unique(mapped$confidence),
      options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
    )

  # Build in a temp directory: saveWidget() leaves a scratch "*_files" folder
  # beside its target even when the result is fully self-contained.
  staged <- file.path(tempdir(), "drc_sentinel_sites_map.html")
  saveWidget(map, staged, selfcontained = TRUE)
  file.copy(staged, file.path(paths$output, "drc_sentinel_sites_map.html"),
            overwrite = TRUE)
  cat("Interactive map saved to: output/drc_sentinel_sites_map.html\n")

  map
} else {
  cat("No sites were successfully geocoded. Map cannot be created.\n")
}
```

## Troubleshooting

### Issue 1: `REQUEST_DENIED` from the API

**Cause**: The key is missing, restricted, or the Geocoding API is not enabled
on the Google Cloud project.

**Solution**: Enable "Geocoding API" at
<https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library>, and check that any HTTP
referrer or IP restrictions on the key permit server-side use.

### Issue 2: A site is rejected for the wrong province

**Cause**: Google returned a result whose `administrative_area_level_1` differs
from the province the query was pinned to. The `components` filter is advisory,
so this happens when the site name matches something better-known elsewhere in
the country — typically a business or street in Kinshasa.

**Solution**: The rejection is correct; a point in the wrong province is
worthless. Check `drc_geocoding_candidates.csv` to see what was offered. If the
site simply is not in Google's data, pin it in `manual_overrides.csv`.

### Issue 3: A site resolves only at rung 3 or 4

**Cause**: The province-constrained rungs returned `ZERO_RESULTS`, or everything
they offered was rejected.

**Solution**: Check the audit trail for what each rung returned. The site name
is most likely spelled differently in Google's data — add a correction to
`site_name_fixes` in `config.R` and re-run.

### Issue 4: A site is rejected as an administrative-area centroid

**Cause**: The health zone is not a named settlement in Google's data, so the
geocoder fell back to the enclosing province or territory.

**Solution**: This rejection is intentional — a province centroid is worse than
no coordinate. Pin the true location in `manual_overrides.csv`.

### Issue 5: Coordinates outside the DRC

**Cause**: Should be impossible given `components=country:CD`. If it occurs, the
`components` parameter is not reaching the API.

**Solution**: Inspect the `components` column in the candidate audit trail.

### Issue 6: The document re-renders without contacting the API

**Cause**: This is the response cache working as intended.

**Solution**: Delete `../cache/google_geocode_cache.rds` to force fresh lookups.

## Output Files

| File | Description | Format |
|------|-------------|--------|
| `drc_sentinel_sites_geocoded.csv` | Input columns plus coordinates and full provenance | CSV |
| `drc_geocoding_candidates.csv` | Every candidate at every rung, accepted or rejected | CSV |
| `drc_geocoding_review.csv` | Anything below `high` confidence | CSV |
| `drc_geocoding_failed.csv` | Sites with no acceptable candidate | CSV |
| `drc_out_of_bounds.csv` | Coordinates outside the DRC (only if any occur) | CSV |
| `drc_sentinel_sites_map.html` | Interactive map | HTML |

## Appendices

### Appendix A: API Documentation

- <a href="https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/geocoding/overview" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">**Google Maps Geocoding API**</a>
- <a href="https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/geocoding/requests-geocoding#component-filtering" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">**Component filtering**</a> — the `country` and `administrative_area` restrictions this pipeline relies on

### Appendix B: DRC Geographic Context

**Administrative structure:**

- 26 provinces since 2015, reorganised from the previous 11
- Provinces are divided into territories, and health services into *zones de santé*
- French is the official language
- Geographic bounds: latitude 13.5°S–5.4°N, longitude 12.0°E–31.4°E

### Appendix C: Caching and Terms of Use

Responses are cached in `../cache/google_geocode_cache.rds` so that
re-rendering costs no API calls and yields identical coordinates. Google Maps
Platform terms permit only limited temporary caching of geocoding results
(place IDs excepted), so this should be treated as a short-lived local
convenience for iteration rather than a permanent store.
